messages:
alex: heads up — i'm going to prototype exposing 'cache lineage' (per-request cache hits + credited token counts) to the console via an internal read-only API. quick sync?

rui: +1. do we intend to expose per-invocation granularity or only aggregated credits? big perf diff.

alex: plan: per-invocation downstream, but only surfaced as aggregated rollups by tenant/route in the console. we keep raw events for 7d and aggregated daily thereafter.

sam: routing note — sticky routing + model fallback will double-count if we naively attribute cache hits to the first route. need stable attribution heuristic.

jess: also: quotas. if we show credited tokens it might confuse billing teams unless we clearly separate 'cache credits' vs billed tokens. UX needs a badge or tooltip.

alex: agreed re: UX. api prototype response (internal):
```json
{"request_id":"r123","route":"/chat","model":"redwood-rl-1","cache_hit":true,"credited_tokens":24,"kv_key":"sha1:abcd"}
```
this is what the telemetry emits. console would post-process.

rui: how about sampling first? streaming every invocation -> storage spike. can we do 1% sampling + deterministic sampling for large tenants?

sam: I like deterministic sampling for tenants > X qps. Also, for rollouts we should expose a per-canary preview (e.g., show expected cost delta if canary at 10% continues).

jess: performance guardrails: if API causes >10% p99 write latency increase for the agent, autoswitch to aggregated-only.

alex: acceptable. i'll add feature flag + canary flag. rollout plan: 1% global sample + deterministic 10% for top 20 tenants. store raw events 7d, aggregate hourly for 30d.

cost-bot: summary: new telemetry API -> cachelineage.v1.read; sampling: 1% global, 10% deterministic top tenants; retention: raw 7d; hourly aggregates 30d; UI work: badge + 'cache credit' column in per-route econ table. :white_check_mark:

rui: can you pid the API schema to eng-platform API spec repo and tag me? I'll run a load estimate.

alex: yep. i'll open a PR today and paste the link here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
